output.summary: Approved G1036 design revision 2 (the whitepaper), built on the owner's interview answers WD1-WD8: docs/WHITEPAPER.md, claim first (deterministic progressive disclosure, distinguished from concept loading), practitioner-first front half and a technical back half, brief related work, ratios and trends only, byline David Rzepa; a blog draft docs/blog/release-1.md that the owner publishes. Every claim has a ledger entry resolved by .agents/whitepaper_check.py against SPEC/DESIGN sections, tests, a nine-step synthetic trace generated by the real CLI, or the dogfood report; the paper names its checked dev build and is re-checked against the Release 1 tag. Written after G1037 merges. Approved after one review round.

Revision 3 narrowly reconciles the whitepaper plan with approved G1037 attempt 5: merge-sync/change-based carry, verification plus base-focused implementation review, per-stage finding budgets and findings preserved across answered owner-question blocks. The trace and evaluation now distinguish real observations, cited tests and unobserved cases across A1–A20; writing explicitly waits for G1037 merge/report even if base is stack-ready earlier. WD1–WD8 and the existing binding, ratio-only evidence, anonymity, byline and external-post boundaries are unchanged; no paper or dogfood outcome is produced in this design phase.

findings.text: Several DESIGN decision ids point at the wrong decisions. In DESIGN §9, D1 is per-goal state branches, D2 the spec location, D3 approve_merge, D4 design approval, D6 implementation strategy, D12 the default graph and D14 code identity. The design's §3 item 7 cites D2 for 'per-goal branches, Git as the only store' (should be D1), D3 for the default graph (should be D12 plus §4.1 as amended), D4 for identities and fingerprints (should be D14 plus §3.4/§3.5), and D6 for releases (should be the release gate, W10 in §2.5 and SPEC release_gate, plus G1025's HISTORY §4 row). Limitation 3 also lists 'the release ceremony (R9)' as lost while §7.8 describes G1025's release lines with approve_finish. Fix: correct the ids and cite sections (or '§9 Dn') in the ledger. Reword R9 as 'the propose/freeze ceremony was removed; G1025 restores release lines without it', checked against G1025's merged contract.

The binding check covers only the engine and templates, so it does not back the paper's claims. §5.1's `git diff --quiet <checked> <tag> -- plugins/zzzops/zzzops ':!**/plugin.json'` misses skills/ and references/, where behaviour the paper describes lives: owner-question batching in the execute skill (G1026), the intent check at capture (G1029) and the policy-update flow (G1024). Its exclusion is a no-op, because plugin.json sits outside that path. G1027's build id hashes the whole PLUGIN_ROOT and release rendering rewrites the manifests and skill metadata, so the header's build id can only be the checked dev build. Fix: diff plugins/zzzops as a whole, excluding only the version-bearing manifests (plugin.json, .codex-plugin/plugin.json, .claude-plugin/plugin.json) and normalising any provenance lines that release rendering rewrites. State in the header that the build id is the checked dev build's, and that the tag statement covers the source.

output.summary: Approved. Both findings are resolved. 1:1: the decision ids now match DESIGN §9 (D1/D2, D7, D11, D12 with §4.1 as amended, D14 with §3.4/§3.5), and the new SPEC citations exist on the g1017 docs (§4.4 CAS, §4.7 identities, §4.8 fingerprints, §4.12 leases, §4.21 carry-forward, §3.1 release_gate). The ledger uses 'DESIGN §9 Dn' and 'DESIGN §5 Rn', checked per row (W14), and R9 is reconciled with G1025. 1:2: the binding diff covers all of plugins/zzzops minus the three version manifests, and the header labels the dev build id and limits the tag statement to the source. All three notes were taken (T1 corrected, ratio rule broadened, fallback for any trace step). No new findings.

spec:
Publish a long-form, linkable, print-friendly whitepaper on the repository's GitHub-hosted docs path, linked from README, that coins deterministic progressive disclosure: a pure frontier derives each agent's next action and a per-node task card disclosing only that node's prompt, selected policy instructions and inputs from Git state. Explain the mechanism as the reset built it: goal documents on per-goal branches with CAS writes, lease branches, the declarative workflow.json graph with review and human approve nodes, findings and corrections, tree/change identities and fingerprint staleness, stacked PRs with carry-forward, policy branches that pause work, and releases. Include one synthetic end-to-end trace and accessible diagrams, and state limitations candidly (advisory routing, no comprehension proof, what R1-R15 gave up). Claims bind to an explicit engine version and are checked against it. Changed from the old wording: drop heartbeats, receipts, storage locks, linear stacks and model-effort binding, and describe the Release 1 lens-based default graph.

Migrated from GitHub issue #490 after the engine reset (#740).

Order (owner, 2026-11-01): "whitepaper should be after dogfood run". Write it after G1037, from the engine as released and the private-app dogfood run notes (real goals, a real release, measured costs), and include the git-flow release branching (G1025), capabilities (G1027) and owner-question interviews (G1026).

Replaces G1002 (its branch was deleted to remove a private name, owner decision 2026-11-01).
title: Write and publish the ZzzOps whitepaper on deterministic progressive disclosure
